channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Head of Gardening Cooperative Arrested for Extorting $100,000
item.description: The head of a gardening cooperative and an alleged accomplice have been arrested in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy region for extorting $100,000 from entrepreneurs. They are accused of threatening business activities if the money was not paid.

item.title: Drunk Driver Evades Police, Collides with Patrol Car in Abai Region
item.description: In the Urzhar district of Abai region, a 62-year-old driver refused to stop for police and attempted to flee. During the pursuit, the driver collided with a patrol car. A sobriety test confirmed the driver was intoxicated. Police have forwarded materials for two offenses to court.

item.title: Kazakh Doctors Collaborate with International Professors on Complex Surgeries
item.description: An international educational course concluded at the Kazakh Research Institute of Oncology and Radiology in Almaty, gathering over 500 local and foreign doctors. Leading specialists shared expertise on complex surgeries, modern diagnostics, and cancer treatment. A live surgery demonstration for stomach cancer was broadcast to regional oncologists.

item.title: Saudi Parliament Speaker Abdullah Al Sheikh Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for Official Visit
item.description: Abdullah Al Sheikh, Speaker of the Shura Council of Saudi Arabia, arrived in Kyrgyzstan on November 22 for an official visit. He is scheduled to hold talks with the Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, Marlen Mamataliev. The visit aims to strengthen bilateral relations, expand cooperation, and enhance inter-parliamentary contacts between the two countries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Billion-Dollar Debt and Governance Challenges, Economy Grows
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's GDP grew 10.5% in Jan-Oct 2026, reaching 1.87 trillion soms. Industrial output rose 5.2%, with annual inflation at 11.1% in October. The EBRD reported a decline in governance quality to 4.34 points, citing press freedom and AML/CFT concerns, though economic stability improved.

item.title: Kazakh Rescuers Showcase New Equipment to Clear Fire Truck Access
item.description: Rescuers in Almaty and Astana demonstrated new equipment designed to move illegally parked cars blocking access for fire trucks. The specialized tools allow emergency services to quickly clear pathways for fire engines and rescue operations, ensuring faster response times.

item.title: Panjshir Youth Face Discrimination in NGO Job Recruitment, Study Finds
item.description: A study by the Panjshir Studies Centre reveals that young people from Panjshir face discrimination in recruitment for NGOs working with international organizations. Out of over 300 employees in Panjshir, only 60 are local residents, with most management positions held by non-Panjshiris. The report highlights preferential hiring and limited access to opportunities for local youth.

item.title: UN Highlights Media's Crucial Role in Fighting Racism and Discrimination
item.description: The United Nations emphasized the media's vital role in combating racism and all forms of discrimination. The UN stated that media can help reduce discrimination and foster coexistence by presenting accurate and diverse societal portrayals. Avoiding discriminatory stereotypes and providing platforms for vulnerable groups to share their voices are key responsibilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan-Kazakhstan Border Truck Congestion Due to Increased Freight Traffic, Customs Says
item.description: Uzbekistan's Customs Committee commented on social media videos showing truck congestion at the border with Kazakhstan. The committee stated that border crossing points are operating normally. However, data from the Turkestan region shows 100 trucks queued at the 'B. Konysbayev' crossing on November 20. The daily flow of trucks has increased significantly, with transit cargo being the main component.

item.title: Uzbekistan and US Discuss Strengthening Strategic Partnership
item.description: A roundtable on "New Uzbekistan and Uzbek-American Strategic Ties" was held in Washington. The event, hosted by the Hudson Institute, included Uzbek delegation members and US experts. Discussions focused on expanding industrial, technological, and regional security cooperation, with a noted increase in US interest in Central Asia.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Train Air Traffic Controllers Using American Programs
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to open a branch of the American Kent State University to train air traffic controllers, pilots, and aviation engineers. An agreement was reached following a meeting between Kazakhstan's Ministry of Transport and the university. The educational center will also serve other Central Asian countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Enter New Phase of Economic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey are strengthening their economic ties, with Turkey being a major trade partner. Trade turnover has grown significantly, exceeding $3 billion by 2025. Turkey's expertise in industry, construction, and textiles, combined with Uzbekistan's resources, forms a basis for mutual benefit.

item.title: New 550 MW thermal power plant in Jizzakh region connected to grid
item.description: A new 550 MW thermal power plant in Uzbekistan's Jizzakh region, built by Turkey's Cengiz Enerji, has begun supplying electricity to the national grid. The plant uses combined cycle gas turbines and is expected to generate 4.4 billion kWh annually, saving 500 million cubic meters of natural gas. The project cost $500 million.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Host Branch of American University for Aviation Specialists
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to open a branch of the American Kent State University, which trains aviation specialists. This new educational center could become a regional hub for pilots, air traffic controllers, and technical staff in Central Asia. The agreement was reached during a meeting between Kazakh officials and the university delegation.

item.title: UNICEF Reports Highest Child Casualties in Ukraine in Nearly Four Years
item.description: UNICEF states that child casualties in Ukraine have reached their highest level in nearly four years, with at least 1,144 children killed or injured in the first 10 months of 2026. This figure surpasses previous years, averaging over three child casualties daily. The organization stresses this situation must not be normalized.

item.title: Afghanistan and Kenya Discuss Expanding Trade and Mining Cooperation
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Industry and Commerce, Nooruddin Azizi, met with Kenya's Minister of Mining, Hassan Ali Joho, on the sidelines of the Tanzania Investment Conference. They discussed expanding trade, economic cooperation, and potential collaboration in mining, mineral processing, and agricultural production. Both sides expressed interest in increasing trade exchanges and improving market access for their respective products.

item.title: Experts Discuss China-US-Russia Summit, Rejecting 'Yalta 2.0' Comparison
item.description: Experts discussed a trilateral meeting between China, the US, and Russia in Shenzhen, rejecting comparisons to the 'Yalta Conference 2.0'. They analyzed potential long-term consequences of the final declaration and the future of the trilateral format, concluding that the meeting did not resemble the historical Yalta conference's division of spheres of influence.

item.title: UN Chief Warns Rising Poverty and Conflicts Threaten Children's Future
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that increasing child poverty, armed conflicts, and climate shocks are jeopardizing children's futures. He called for stronger action to protect children's rights and ensure access to essential services like healthcare and education, emphasizing the need for sustained investment and commitment to their well-being and development.

item.title: Taliban and Kenya Discuss Expansion of Trade and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Industry and Commerce, Nooruddin Azizi, met with Kenya's Minister of Mining, Hassan Ali Joho, to discuss expanding trade relations. Discussions included cooperation in mining, mineral processing, exports, and agricultural production.

item.title: Iran Confirms Qatari Delegation Visited Tehran for Nuclear Talks
item.description: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi confirmed a Qatari delegation visited Tehran to discuss ending the war with the US. He stated that Iran is in contact with mediators, including Qatar, to explore diplomatic opportunities.

item.title: Hazara Activists Urge European Parliament to Halt Persecution and Land Seizures
item.description: A Hazara delegation presented a dossier on alleged genocide to the European Parliament, calling for action against ethnic persecution, forced displacement, and land grabbing. They met with MEP Javier López in Brussels on Friday. The activists requested EU political and legal support to stop human rights violations and prevent forced returns to Afghanistan.

item.title: Video Surfaces of Azerbaijan Airlines Plane Crash Near Aktau
item.description: A full video of an Embraer 190 aircraft from Azerbaijan Airlines, which crashed near Aktau, has circulated on social media. The footage shows the plane flying at a low altitude before crashing and catching fire. Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev pledged full efforts to investigate the incident.

item.title: UK Government Concerned Over Potential New US Military Action Against Iran
item.description: The UK government and senior officials are discussing the possibility of renewed large-scale US military strikes against Iran. Potential Iranian retaliation is also a cause for concern for high-ranking British officials.

item.title: Melania Trump Negotiating Ceasefire Between Russia and Ukraine Before Christmas
item.description: First Lady Melania Trump stated she is negotiating a new ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, potentially achievable before Christmas on December 25. She expressed a desire for world peace and more ceasefires, indicating ongoing talks.

item.title: Two Former Commanders Arrested in Connection with Kyrgyz Military Helicopter Crash
item.description: Two former commanders of the Kyrgyz Air Force, including ex-commander Kylychbek Aidaraliev and a unit commander Daniyar Davitahunov, have been arrested. They face charges related to violating flight safety regulations, leading to a fatal Mi-8MTV helicopter crash in January 2024. Both have been detained until December 2026.

item.title: Taliban Minister of Industry and Commerce meets Tanzania's Minister of Minerals to boost trade
item.description: Nooruddin Azizi, the Taliban's Minister of Industry and Commerce, met with Tanzania's Minister of Minerals, Anthony Mavunde, to discuss expanding bilateral trade. Discussions included exporting Afghan agricultural products, carpets, and minerals to Tanzania, and holding trade exhibitions. Processing mineral resources within Afghanistan was also considered.

item.title: Taliban Claim Over 200 Media Outlets Licensed in Past Five Years
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Information and Culture claims over 200 media outlets have received operating licenses in Afghanistan in the last five years. A spokesperson stated the ministry is launching programs to support media growth and improve journalists' capacities. However, many media outlets have shut down and journalists lost jobs since the Taliban's return to power.

item.title: Moscow Reviews Efforts to Resolve Afghanistan-Pakistan Tensions
item.description: Discussions were held in Moscow regarding efforts to resolve tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan. The review of these diplomatic efforts took place amidst ongoing regional developments and bilateral relations between the two neighboring countries.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence Development and Digital Space Protection Discussed
item.description: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence presents both opportunities and challenges. While AI is increasingly integrated into various sectors, concerns arise regarding data privacy, misinformation, deepfakes, and cyberattacks. International cooperation is deemed crucial for regulating AI, balancing innovation with human rights and digital security.

item.title: Uzbekneftegaz to Double Gasoline Supply to Exchange Amid Rising Demand
item.description: Uzbekneftegaz plans to increase daily gasoline supply to the exchange to 8,000 tons, potentially up to 10,000 tons if demand continues to grow. The company currently offers 4,600 tons daily. This move aims to stabilize prices, which have been influenced by increased demand and precautionary buying by gas stations.

item.title: Documentary Evidence of Hazara Genocide and Forced Displacement Presented to European Parliament
item.description: Documentary evidence and reports concerning the 'genocide' and forced displacement of the Hazara people have been presented to the European Parliament. The specific details of the presentation and the content of the evidence were not disclosed.

item.title: Mass Youth Protests Erupt Across Over 25 European Countries
item.description: Tens of thousands of young people have protested in over 25 European countries against the rising cost of living, tuition fees, and underfunding of education. Protesters demanded increased funding for schools and universities, better living conditions, and action against unemployment and climate change. Some protests involved property damage.

item.title: Modern Youth Face New Challenges in Pursuit of Financial Independence and Housing
item.description: Today's youth, despite greater access to education and information, face significant hurdles to financial independence. High competition, job scarcity, and the difficulty of gaining experience delay financial self-sufficiency. Additionally, rising housing costs and rents make homeownership increasingly unattainable for many young people.

item.title: Russia Urges Regional Cooperation Against Afghan Militant Groups
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated that militant groups like ISKP and TTP remain active in Afghanistan, posing a regional security threat. Moscow advocates for a common goal in counter-terrorism, emphasizing economic development and institutional strengthening in Afghanistan. Russia also supports a diplomatic solution to tensions between Pakistan and the Taliban government.

item.title: Europe's Generation Z Protests Rising Costs, Education Funding, and Gaza Conflict
item.description: Young people across 25 European countries have taken to the streets to protest against the rising cost of living, increased tuition fees, and underfunding of education. Protesters also voiced opposition to their governments' stances on the conflict in Gaza.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Recalculate Electricity Bills for Homes Lacking Gas Supply from November 25
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy announced that electricity bills for residents in areas without gas supply will be recalculated starting November 25. This adjustment follows complaints about the standard electricity tariff being applied instead of the preferential rate for unsupplied gas areas.

item.title: Astana Hospitals See Surge in Respiratory Illnesses, Primarily Affecting Children
item.description: Astana is experiencing a rise in acute respiratory viral infections and influenza cases, with 313 patients currently hospitalized. A significant majority, 220, are children, and 30 are pregnant women. Hospital bed capacity has been increased, and emergency services are operating on an enhanced schedule.

item.title: Former Khorezm Employment Center Official Detained in Turkey
item.description: A citizen of Uzbekistan, wanted internationally, has been detained in Turkey. The former official from the Khorezm Region Employment Promotion Center is accused of embezzling state funds and falsifying documents. She was apprehended through a joint operation by Uzbek and Turkish law enforcement.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Seeks International Fugitive
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has placed a 45-year-old foreign national, Williams Cole, on an international wanted list for illegally crossing the state border. The case is registered in the Turkestan region, with the Saragash district police department handling the search. The suspect was born in 1981, but his nationality and further details remain undisclosed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Increases Preferential Electricity Tariff for Undersupplied Areas
item.description: Starting November 1, households in areas not supplied with natural gas or with limited gas supply in Uzbekistan will pay 650 soums per kilowatt-hour for electricity up to 350 kWh. This preferential rate will be applied automatically without requiring additional applications. The change aims to support residents in regions facing gas shortages.
